readme.title: What this module covers
readme.html:
What this module covers

This module explains what cloud migration is and the three phases a large migration goes through: assess, mobilize, and migrate and modernize. It introduces the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework with its six perspectives, and the seven migration strategies. It then matches AWS services to each job: four services for applications, AWS DMS and AWS SCT for databases, and DataSync, Transfer Family, Direct Connect and Snowball Edge for data.

readme.title: Lessons
readme.html:
Lessons

Module 12 Introduction

  1. Introduction to Migration: what cloud migration is and the three phases with their supporting services.

Migration Frameworks and Strategies

  1. AWS Cloud Adoption Framework: AWS CAF, its benefits, its six perspectives and the AWS CAF Action Plan.
  2. Seven Migration Strategies: the seven Rs, from relocate to retire, and when each one fits.

Migration Services and Tools

  1. Migration Services and Tools: Migration Evaluator, Application Discovery Service, Migration Hub, Application Migration Service and competency partners, compared side by side.

Migrating Databases to the AWS Cloud

  1. Database Migrations: homogeneous and heterogeneous moves, and when to use AWS DMS or AWS SCT.

Migrating Data to the AWS Cloud

  1. Transferring Data Online: DataSync, Transfer Family and Direct Connect for online transfers.
  2. Transferring Data Offline: Snowball Edge Storage Optimized devices for offline, multi-petabyte moves.

readme.title: Key takeaways
readme.html:
Key takeaways

  • Cloud migration is rarely one and done; large moves follow three sequential phases: assess, mobilize, then migrate and modernize.
  • AWS CAF organizes its guidance into six perspectives and also provides tools to speed the move: Business, People and Governance on the business side, Platform, Security and Operations on the technical side.
  • The People perspective drives organization-wide change management, and the Platform perspective covers architecture and moving workloads.
  • Organizations often combine the seven Rs: relocate, rehost, replatform, refactor, repurchase, retain, retire.
  • Migration Evaluator prices the move for the business case, Application Discovery Service inventories servers and dependencies, Migration Hub tracks everything in one free place, and Application Migration Service moves and modernizes applications.
  • AWS DMS moves databases with low downtime while the source stays live, and AWS SCT converts schemas and code objects when the target engine differs.
  • DataSync manages most online data migrations with scheduling and task reporting, Transfer Family runs managed file transfers over protocols like SFTP and FTPS, and Direct Connect only supplies a dedicated link.
  • Snowball Edge Storage Optimized devices move data offline when bandwidth, connectivity or sheer volume rules out an online transfer.

readme.title: What the assessment focuses on
readme.html:
What the assessment focuses on

The module assessment has 9 questions.

  • AWS Cloud Adoption Framework: 3 questions, on which perspective owns organization-wide change management, on the framework's purpose, and with its perspectives as a distractor among the strategies.
  • Seven migration strategies: 2 questions, once as the answer and once as a distractor about AWS CAF.
  • Three migration phases: 1 question, as a distractor next to the seven Rs.
  • AWS Migration Hub: 5 questions, the answer once (central view of tasks and progress) and a distractor in the other four.
  • Migration Evaluator: 4 questions, the answer once (business case) and a distractor in the other three.
  • AWS Application Migration Service: 3 questions, the answer once (moving apps while modernizing and cutting cost) and a distractor in the other two.
  • AWS Application Discovery Service: 3 questions, always a distractor, since an inventory of servers and dependencies is neither a business case, a central tracking hub nor an app-moving tool.
  • AWS DMS: 2 questions, the answer once as the end-to-end database migration tool and described in one distractor.
  • AWS SCT: 1 question, a distractor because it converts schemas and code but does not run the whole migration.
  • AWS DataSync: 2 questions, the answer once (managed, scheduled online transfer with reporting) and a distractor once.
  • AWS Transfer Family: 2 questions, the answer once (managed file transfer over several protocols) and a distractor once.
  • Snowball Edge Storage Optimized devices: 2 questions, both distractors because they move data offline.
  • AWS Direct Connect and virtual private gateways: 1 question each, as distractors for online data transfer.

readme.title: Summary
readme.html:
Summary

Planning a move to AWS starts with readiness and people, which the six AWS CAF perspectives organize, and follows three phases: assess, mobilize, and migrate and modernize. Each application then gets one of the seven Rs, anywhere from relocating it to retiring it. Finally, AWS services do the moving: Application Migration Service for applications, AWS DMS and AWS SCT for databases, and DataSync, Transfer Family, Direct Connect or Snowball Edge for data.

introduction-to-migration.html:
Introduction to Migration

Objectives

  • Define .
  • Name the three phases of a large migration.

Notes

Cloud migration

  • Moving apps, databases and other IT resources from on premises or another cloud to AWS.
  • It takes planning, the move and upkeep, often in iterative stages AWS supports.

The three phases

  • Assess: gauge readiness, set outcomes, goals and the need to move, then weigh findings into a business case ().
  • Mobilize: ready the organization and resources, write the plan around app dependencies, close readiness gaps and pick strategies (Application Discovery Service, Migration Hub).
  • Migrate and modernize: architect, migrate and validate each app, alone or with specialists and competency partners.
  • Last-phase tools: Application Migration Service, , Migration Hub, and DataSync, Transfer Family or the Snow Family for data.

Visuals

  • Three-phase graphic: a numbered marker per phase with its services.

Key takeaways

  • Order: assess, mobilize, migrate and modernize.
  • Assess yields the business case; mobilize, the plan.
  • Migration is iterative, not one and done.

Terms

  • Cloud migration: Moving IT resources from on premises or another cloud to AWS.
  • Assess phase: Checking readiness and building the business case.
  • Mobilize phase: Preparing the organization and writing the migration plan.
  • Migrate and modernize phase: Moving and validating each app.

aws-cloud-adoption-framework.html:
AWS Cloud Adoption Framework

Objectives

  • Explain why exists and who built it.
  • Match the six perspectives to their focus and roles.

Notes

Why AWS CAF exists

  • Developers, architects and analysts see migration differently, and newcomers may miss a role.
  • built AWS CAF to merge those views, align everyone, field the right team and make the move quick and smooth.
  • It shares AWS experience and best practices, plus tooling that speeds the journey, organizes resources and aligns leaders.
  • Payoffs: revenue, productivity and customer experience up, operating costs and risk down, sustainability and transparency up.
  • Uses: legacy infrastructure and app moves, process and operations changes, and new business models.
  • Exam guide update verified 2026-10-09, AWS Cloud Adoption Framework AWS CAF ties cloud adoption to four business outcomes: reduced business risk, improved ESG performance, increased revenue and increased operational efficiency.

The six perspectives

  • Business, People and Governance are business capabilities; Platform, Security and Operations are technical.
Focus Typical roles
Business IT serves business needs and IT spending ties to key business results; build the business case, rank cloud initiatives, align goals Business and finance managers, budget owners, strategy stakeholders
People Organization-wide change management; review structures, roles, skills and gaps to set training, staffing and org priorities HR, staffing, people managers
Governance Align IT and business strategy for more value and less risk; update skills and processes, measure cloud investments CIO, program and portfolio managers, enterprise architects, business analysts
Platform Patterns for new cloud solutions and moving on-premises workloads; architectural models, detailed target state CTO, IT managers, solutions architects
Security Visibility, auditability, control and agility; choose and implement security controls CISO, IT security managers and analysts
Operations Enable, run, use, operate and recover workloads at the level agreed with business stakeholders; set daily to yearly routines, support business operations, define current procedures plus needed process changes and training IT operations and support managers
  • Course mapping: a business or finance analyst to Business (Governance also lists business analysts), HR to People, a cloud architect to Platform.

AWS CAF Action Plan

  • Skill and process gaps found per perspective feed the , which guides change management.

Visuals

  • Six perspectives image: the six areas, each detailed in an accordion.

Key takeaways

  • AWS CAF organizes guidance into six perspectives and also supplies tools to speed migration.
  • People owns change management; Platform owns architecture and moving workloads.
  • Perspective gaps feed the AWS CAF Action Plan.

Terms

  • AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF): AWS migration guidance in six perspectives, plus tools to speed the move.
  • Perspective: One AWS CAF area with its own stakeholders.
  • AWS CAF Action Plan: A plan built from perspective gaps to steer change management.

seven-migration-strategies.html:
Seven Migration Strategies

Objectives

  • Tell the seven Rs apart and pick the one that fits a given application.

Notes

How to choose a strategy

  • Each app gets one of seven paths, chosen by complexity, goals, time, resources, starting point and future plans.
  • Organizations often combine them into a tailored plan with less risk and disruption.

The seven Rs

Strategy Also called What happens Trade-off or example
- VMs or containers already running on premises move to a cloud host -
Lift and shift Apps move as they are, often servers turned into VMs, with no changes at first Misses some benefits, yet can cut total costs by up to 30 percent; most apps in a legacy migration that must scale fast
Lift, tinker and shift A few cloud optimizations for a tangible gain, without new code or architecture changes MySQL to unchanged, or to , helping the database team and performance
Re-architect New code and cloud-built features, driven by a strong need for features, scale or performance Big payoff, but the highest upfront planning and staff effort
Drop and shop A traditional license swapped for , often a new vendor and a fresh start A database license dropped for cloud databases, or a CRM replaced by new sales force software; the new package can be slow to adopt and cost more upfront
Stays where it lays Business-critical apps stay in the source environment for now: those needing major refactoring, work that can wait, or apps months from deprecation Migrate only what makes business sense; these in place later
Retire - Unneeded apps are switched off Often over 10 percent of a portfolio is unused; ending it saves cost and effort

Visuals

  • Seven strategies diagram: apps pass through discovery and are sorted into the seven Rs, one marker each.

Key takeaways

  • Rehost changes nothing, replatform adds small optimizations, and refactor writes new code at the highest upfront cost.
  • Repurchase trades licensed software for SaaS, often from a new vendor.
  • Retain and retire involve no migration.

Scenarios

  • Legacy estate that must scale fast: rehost.
  • MySQL to Amazon RDS with no code changes: replatform.

Terms

  • Relocate: Moving existing VMs or containers to the cloud.
  • Rehost: Moving apps to AWS unchanged.
  • Replatform: Moving apps with small cloud optimizations.
  • Refactor: Rebuilding an app with new code and cloud-built features.
  • Repurchase: Replacing licensed software with SaaS.
  • Retain: Keeping business-critical apps where they are for now.
  • Retire: Shutting down apps no longer needed.

Migration Services and Tools

Objectives

  • Tell apart the four core migration services and the phase each serves.
  • Know when to use , Application Discovery Service, Migration Hub or Application Migration Service.
  • Know where to find partner help.

Notes

The four services side by side

Service Phase Nickname What you get Pick it when
Migration Evaluator Assess Moving consultant A data-driven business case: current versus target state, a readiness plan, projected cloud costs The spend must be justified and budgeted
Mobilize Detective An automatic inventory of on-premises servers, databases and links, feeding a detailed migration plan Inventory and dependencies are unknown
Mobilize, then migrate and modernize Command center One free place to discover, assess, plan, execute and track, with guidance and automated recommendations The team needs every task and its progress in one view
Migrate and modernize Expert movers Apps replicated to AWS faster, for less and with minimal downtime, optionally modernized You are ready to move the apps themselves
  • Together: fewer errors and less downtime, planning savings, a simpler process, faster cloud value.

Partner help

  • The AWS Competency Partner Program lists migration partners by phase or kind of help: see AWS Migration and Modernization Competency Partners.

Visuals

  • Phase banners: one image each for assess, mobilize, and migrate and modernize.
  • Mover cartoon: a mover expects to haul only the app, but a compute resource and a database insist on coming, so dependencies travel together.
  • Hub cartoon: a technician among status screens reports the migration is on track, picturing Migration Hub.

Key takeaways

  • Memory aid: Discovery Service inventories, Evaluator prices, Hub tracks, Application Migration Service moves.
  • Migration Hub is free and spans mobilize through migrate and modernize.
  • Application Migration Service moves and modernizes apps faster and cheaper.
  • Competency partners fill expertise gaps.

Scenarios

  • Finance wants projected AWS costs before approving: Migration Evaluator.
  • Nobody knows which servers an app relies on: AWS Application Discovery Service.
  • Leaders want live status for every workstream: AWS Migration Hub.

Terms

  • Migration Evaluator: An assessment service that builds a cost-backed business case.
  • AWS Application Discovery Service: A service that inventories on-premises servers and their connections.
  • AWS Migration Hub: A free central hub for planning and tracking a migration.
  • AWS Application Migration Service: A service that moves apps to AWS and can modernize them.
  • AWS Migration and Modernization Competency Partners: AWS partners specializing in migration phases or needs.

database-migrations.html:
Database Migrations

Objectives

  • Explain why changing database engines complicates a migration.
  • Know what and each do and when to choose them.

Notes

Migration types

  • Databases move to cut costs or modernize, a chance to redesign them; AWS managed or open source targets can lower licensing costs.
  • Homogeneous: the same engine on both ends, so fairly simple.
  • Heterogeneous: a new engine, such as legacy commercial to , which is harder and may need app changes.
  • A heterogeneous move must recreate the , the database's blueprint (tables, field types, relationships), which is slow by hand.

How AWS DMS works

  • It moves relational and NoSQL databases, data warehouses and analytics workloads to AWS.
  • You name the source and target, and a scheduled task on a replication VM copies the data while the source stays live.
  • You can fall back to the original or replicate into other Regions or Availability Zones.
  • Exam guide update verified 2026-10-09, What is AWS DMS? With database replication, AWS DMS goes beyond a one-time copy and keeps replicating ongoing changes from the source database to the target so the two stay in sync.

AWS DMS versus AWS SCT

AWS DMS AWS SCT
Job Moves and replicates data; covers planning, assessment, conversion and the move itself Converts schemas and code objects (stored procedures, views, functions) to a new engine
Strengths Low downtime, , both migration types, low-cost terabyte moves Flags manual work, estimates effort, automates analysis at scale, works with popular engines
Uses Managed databases, dropping licenses, ongoing replication, integration Commercial to open source, big data warehouses, updating schemas in place
  • Both save time and money, ease adopting new databases and follow AWS security best practices.

Visuals

  • Bird cartoon: birds lifting a database to the cloud are unsure where it goes, so they reach for AWS SCT.

Key takeaways

  • AWS DMS keeps the source live and handles both migration types.
  • AWS SCT helps heterogeneous moves by converting schema and code, saving weeks or months.
  • Rule: schema or code conversion points to SCT; moving data or one end-to-end tool points to DMS.

Scenarios

  • Commercial database to Amazon Aurora: AWS SCT converts schema and code, then AWS DMS moves the data.

Terms

  • AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS): A service that migrates and replicates databases to AWS.
  • AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT): A tool that converts schemas and code objects between engines.
  • Homogeneous migration: A move between databases on the same engine.
  • Heterogeneous migration: A move to a database on a different engine.
  • Schema: The blueprint of a database's tables, field types and relationships.

transferring-data-online.html:
Transferring Data Online

Objectives

  • Match online transfer needs to DataSync, Transfer Family or Direct Connect, with offline (lesson 7) as the fallback.

Notes

Before moving data

  • Check safety, integrity, timing and bandwidth.
  • Databases use ; DataSync suits most other data.

AWS DataSync

  • Automates and speeds large, secure moves from on-premises storage into AWS storage like .
  • It handles instances, encryption and network tuning, and lets you throttle, schedule, filter and report on tasks.

AWS Transfer Family

  • Fully managed file transfer in and out of Amazon S3 and over FTP, SFTP, FTPS and other transfer protocols.
  • It adds encryption and authentication with less infrastructure to manage.

AWS Direct Connect

  • A dedicated private line to a VPC (networking module) that adds bandwidth and can cut network costs.
  • It is only the path; DataSync still manages the move.

Visuals

  • Four businesses illustration: each has one transfer worry (scheduling, bandwidth, validation, security).

Key takeaways

  • DataSync manages most data moves, with scheduling and task reports.
  • Transfer Family does managed, protocol-based file transfer.
  • Direct Connect is a link, not a migration manager.

Terms

  • AWS DataSync: A service that automates data transfer into AWS storage.
  • AWS Transfer Family: A managed multi-protocol file transfer service.
  • Transfer protocol: A rule set for how data moves between places.
  • AWS Direct Connect: A dedicated private network link to AWS.

transferring-data-offline.html:
Transferring Data Offline

Objectives

  • Know when to ship data on a device instead of the network.
  • Describe Snowball Edge Storage Optimized devices.

Notes

When to go offline

  • Many customers prefer online moves; offline means sending data on a physical device when DataSync falls short.
  • Triggers: thin bandwidth, remote sites without internet or Direct Connect, or petabytes that ship faster than they upload.

Snowball Edge Storage Optimized devices

  • devices with NVMe storage for multi-petabyte moves from on-premises sites where internet may be unavailable.
  • They bring strong compute, large capacity and gigabytes per second, and also serve rugged, secure .
  • Being offline, they do not fit online transfer needs.

Visuals

  • Polar bear cartoon: workers on snowmobiles flee a polar bear near a remote research station, amazed at how fast Snowball Edge devices are.

Key takeaways

  • Go offline when bandwidth, connectivity or volume rules out online transfer.
  • Snowball Edge carries multi-petabyte moves and doubles as a rugged edge device.
  • It does not fit online transfer.

Terms

  • Offline data transfer: Moving data to AWS on a physical device.
  • AWS Snow Family: The AWS device family for offline transfer, including Snowball Edge.
  • Snowball Edge Storage Optimized device: An NVMe device for offline, multi-petabyte moves.
  • Edge computing: A Snowball Edge use case that calls for a secure, rugged device.

The cloud architect drawing the detailed target design for the moved order system
Choosing patterns for new cloud apps and for moving the back-room servers
Choosing and putting in place the controls that guard customer card data
The CISO's analysts needing visibility and an audit trail across every cafe account
The IT support manager setting the daily to yearly routines that keep the order app running
Running and recovering the loyalty app at the level agreed with the owner, with the procedures to match

goals.label: The case for the move and oversight of its value sit in Business and Governance
goals.hint: Ask whether the task argues for the move and ties spending to results, or oversees the investment for value and risk.

goals.label: Staff skills and organizational change sit under People
goals.hint: Ask whether the task is about the staff themselves, their structures, roles and skills, and the change they live through.

goals.label: Design and protection tasks sit under Platform and Security
goals.hint: Ask whether the task shapes what gets built and moved, or decides how it is controlled, seen and audited.

goals.label: Keeping workloads running and recovering sits under Operations
goals.hint: Ask whether the task keeps a workload running day to day and year to year, at the level the owner agreed.

lines: Business, People and Governance are the business capabilities of AWS CAF, and Platform, Security and Operations are the technical ones.
Business ties IT spending to the cafe's results and builds the case, while Governance measures the cloud investments for more value and less risk.
People owns change management across the whole chain, reviewing roles and skill gaps to set training priorities.

The technical perspectives split the work: Platform shapes what gets built and moved, Security chooses the controls and keeps it all visible and auditable, and Operations runs and recovers it at the level agreed with the owner.

questions.takeaway: Building the business case and ranking cloud initiatives by business results belongs to the AWS CAF Business perspective.

read.text: IT serves business needs and IT spending ties to key business results; build the business case, rank cloud initiatives, align goals

questions.stem: The cafe's owner wants a written case for funding the cloud move, with cloud initiatives ranked by how much they help sales and IT spending tied to key results. Which AWS CAF perspective covers this work?

options.why: Governance aligns IT and business strategy and measures investments, but it does not build the business case.
Platform designs architecture and target-state patterns, not the case for spending.
The Business perspective builds the business case, ranks cloud initiatives and ties IT spend to results.
Operations runs and recovers workloads day to day, not business case planning.

questions.takeaway: Aligning IT with business strategy and measuring cloud investments points to the AWS CAF Governance perspective.

read.text: Align IT and business strategy for more value and less risk; update skills and processes, measure cloud investments

questions.stem: The cafe chain's CIO wants each cloud investment measured and the IT team's skills and processes updated, so the move adds value while limiting risk. Which AWS CAF perspective fits this goal?

options.why: People leads change management and staffing, not measuring cloud investments against value and risk.
Operations runs and recovers workloads at agreed levels, not measuring cloud investments.
Governance aligns IT and business strategy for more value and less risk and measures cloud investments.
Security picks and implements controls, not strategy alignment or investment measurement.

questions.takeaway: The CTO and solutions architects map to the AWS CAF Platform perspective.

read.text: CTO, IT managers, solutions architects

questions.stem: In AWS CAF, the CTO, IT managers and solutions architects are the typical stakeholders of which perspective?

options.why: People typically involves HR and staffing roles rather than technical architects.
Business typically involves finance managers and budget owners, not solutions architects.
The CTO, IT managers and solutions architects are the typical Platform stakeholders.
Operations typically involves IT operations and support managers rather than the CTO.

incidents.title: New shops bring old servers
incidents.brief: The cafe chain has bought a handful of small coffee shops, each with its own aging servers in a back room. The owner wants them all running on AWS before the holiday rush, but the bank wants to see the numbers first.

steps.takeaway: When a lender or finance team needs projected AWS costs and a current versus target view, Migration Evaluator builds that case.

read.text: A data-driven business case: current versus target state, a readiness plan, projected cloud costs

steps.stem: Before it lends the cafe chain money for the move, the bank asks for projected monthly AWS costs and a comparison of the shops' current setup with the planned one. Which service produces this?

options.why: Migration Hub tracks the tasks and progress of a move, and it does not build the cost-backed case the bank wants.
Migration Evaluator builds a data-driven business case that compares current and target state and projects cloud costs.
Discovery Service lists the shops' servers and their links for the plan, but it does not project the costs.
This service moves the apps once the plan is ready, long after the bank needs its numbers.

steps.takeaway: To plan moves around app dependencies, AWS Application Discovery Service inventories servers, databases and the links between them.

read.text: An automatic inventory of on-premises servers, databases and links, feeding a detailed migration plan

steps.stem: The cafe chain's planner wants to group the new shops' servers into move waves, so that no app ever moves without the database and servers it relies on. Which service gives the planner the data to build those groups?

options.why: Evaluator prices the move as a business case, and it does not record which servers each app relies on.
This service carries the apps across once the waves exist, so it cannot supply the data to form them.
AWS DMS copies database data into AWS, and it does not trace which servers an app depends on.
Discovery Service inventories the servers, databases and the links between them, which is what the wave plan needs.

steps.takeaway: Turning physical servers into VMs on AWS with no app changes is rehost, while relocate moves VMs or containers that already exist.

read.text: Apps move as they are, often servers turned into VMs, with no changes at first

steps.stem: The new shops run their apps directly on physical servers. The team will turn each server into a virtual machine on AWS and leave the apps unchanged for now. Which strategy is this?

options.why: Relocate moves VMs or containers that already exist on premises, and these shops run physical servers.
Replatform adds a few cloud optimizations, but this team is changing nothing in the apps yet.
Rehost moves apps as they are, often by turning servers into VMs, with no changes at first.
Refactor writes new code with cloud-built features, the opposite of leaving the apps as they are.

steps.takeaway: Copying the servers that run the apps into AWS, with optional modernizing, is AWS Application Migration Service, while DMS and DataSync move data.

read.text: Apps replicated to AWS faster, for less and with minimal downtime, optionally modernized

steps.stem: With the plan approved, the team must now copy the servers that run the shops' stock and scheduling software into AWS, keeping downtime short and perhaps modernizing along the way. The databases and file shares are being moved by other tools. Which service should carry those servers across?

options.why: AWS DMS moves and replicates databases, which the team is already handling apart from the apps.
This service replicates the servers and their apps to AWS with minimal downtime and can modernize them along the way.
DataSync moves stored data such as file shares into AWS storage, not the running apps themselves.
Discovery Service inventories the servers and their links to feed the plan, but it does not copy them into AWS.

incidents.title: Leaving the old order database engine
incidents.brief: The cafe's order database runs on a costly commercial engine, and the owner wants it on Amazon Aurora to drop the license. The registers ring up orders all day, and years of custom database code live inside the old engine.

steps.takeaway: Changing engines makes a migration heterogeneous, so the schema must be recreated and the app may need changes.

read.text: Heterogeneous: a new engine, such as legacy commercial to Amazon Aurora, which is harder and may need app changes.

steps.stem: The cafe plans to move its order database from a commercial engine to Amazon Aurora. Which extra tasks does this change of engine add to the move? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Recreating the database schema on Aurora
options.why: A new engine means the tables, field types and relationships must be rebuilt for it, which is slow by hand.

options.text: Copying the existing order rows to Aurora
options.why: Every database move copies the data, even one between the same engine, so the switch of engine does not add it.

options.text: Changing parts of the app that use the data
options.why: Switching to a different engine can require app changes, which a same-engine move usually avoids.

options.text: Naming the source and the target databases
options.why: Any move with AWS DMS starts by naming the source and target, whether or not the engine changes.

options.text: Choosing when the registers switch over
options.why: Every move needs a moment when the registers start using the new database, so this is not extra work from the new engine.

steps.takeaway: AWS SCT converts schemas and code objects to a new engine and flags and estimates the manual work that remains.

read.text: Converts schemas and code objects (stored procedures, views, functions) to a new engine

steps.stem: Before moving the order database to Amazon Aurora, the cafe's team wants to know how much of its stored procedures, views and functions will need manual work, with an estimate of the effort. Which AWS offering fits?

options.why: AWS DMS moves and replicates the data, while sizing up the code objects for a new engine is a conversion task.
Evaluator projects the cost of the whole move, not the effort to convert stored procedures and views.
AWS SCT converts code objects to the new engine and flags and estimates the work it cannot do on its own.
Discovery Service inventories servers and their links, and it does not inspect stored procedures for conversion.

steps.takeaway: AWS DMS copies data while the source stays live and keeps replicating changes so the source and target stay in sync.

read.text: You name the source and target, and a scheduled task on a replication VM copies the data while the source stays live.

steps.stem: With the schema converted, the cafe will use AWS DMS to move its order data to Amazon Aurora. The registers must keep taking orders during the copy, and Aurora must hold every order placed until the cutover. Which AWS DMS capabilities meet these two needs? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Moves relational and NoSQL databases alike
options.why: Support for both database kinds is true of AWS DMS, but it neither keeps the registers running nor captures new orders.

options.text: Copies the data while the source stays live
options.why: The replication task copies the order rows while the old database keeps taking orders from the registers.

options.text: Can place a replica in another AWS Region
options.why: Replicating into another Region is a real option, but it does not keep orders flowing or bring new ones to Aurora.

options.text: Keeps sending new changes to the target
options.why: Ongoing replication carries each order placed during the copy into Aurora, so the two databases match at cutover.

options.text: Handles both same-engine and new-engine moves
options.why: Covering both migration types is true of AWS DMS, but it says nothing about live registers or orders placed mid-copy.

incidents.title: Files, a flour supplier and a far roastery
incidents.brief: The cafe is moving its file data to AWS. The head office has a big file share, the flour supplier still trades files the old-fashioned way, and years of roasting records sit at a roastery in the hills.

steps.takeaway: Direct Connect only supplies the path, and AWS DataSync still schedules, runs and reports on the data move.

read.text: It is only the path; DataSync still manages the move.

steps.stem: The cafe has just added an AWS Direct Connect link from its head office to AWS. The IT lead expects the link alone to copy the office file share into Amazon S3 on a schedule and report on each run. Which service does the cafe still need to manage the move?

options.why: Transfer Family runs protocol-based file exchange such as SFTP, not scheduled bulk copies with run reports.
Snow Family ships data on a device, which a site with a fast private link to AWS does not need.
AWS DMS moves databases, and this job is a file share headed for Amazon S3.
Direct Connect is only the path, and DataSync schedules, runs and reports on the copy over it.

steps.takeaway: Partners that trade files with Amazon S3 or Amazon EFS over FTP, SFTP or FTPS point to AWS Transfer Family.

read.text: Fully managed file transfer in and out of Amazon S3 and Amazon EFS over FTP, SFTP, FTPS and other transfer protocols.

steps.stem: The cafe's flour supplier sends delivery notes over FTPS and wants to pick up the weekly order files that the cafe keeps in Amazon EFS. The cafe would rather avoid running its own file server for this. Which service fits?

options.why: DataSync moves the cafe's own storage into AWS, and it gives the supplier no FTPS endpoint to use.
Transfer Family runs managed FTPS transfers in and out of Amazon EFS, so no file server is needed.
Direct Connect is a private link for the cafe's network, not a managed file exchange for a supplier.
Snow Family ships data on a device, which does not suit a weekly file exchange with a supplier.

steps.takeaway: No connectivity, thin bandwidth or petabytes that ship faster than they upload point to offline transfer on a device.

read.text: Triggers: thin bandwidth, remote sites without internet or Direct Connect, or petabytes that ship faster than they upload.

steps.stem: The cafe checks each of its sites before moving data to AWS. Which findings point to shipping the data on a physical device instead of sending it over the network? (Select TWO.)

options.text: The head office reaches AWS over a private Direct Connect line
options.why: A private link gives the head office a network path to AWS, so its data can move online.

options.text: The roastery has neither internet service nor a Direct Connect line
options.why: With no network path at all, the roastery's records can only reach AWS on a device.

options.text: The flour supplier sends its delivery notes to the cafe only over FTPS
options.why: A transfer protocol is an online need that a managed file exchange serves, not a reason to ship a device.

options.text: The back office photo archive would take months over its thin line
options.why: When a thin line would take months, a device delivers the archive to AWS sooner.

options.text: The sales files must reach AWS every night, with no end date planned
options.why: A nightly copy that never ends is an ongoing online need, which a device does not fit.

incidents.title: The move plan stalls
incidents.brief: Halfway through planning its move to AWS, the cafe chain hits trouble. Baristas are uneasy about new systems, and the team still has not settled what to do with the loyalty database, the staff rota software and the payroll app.

steps.takeaway: Staff fears, training and role changes during a cloud move belong to the AWS CAF People perspective and its change management.

read.text: Organization-wide change management; review structures, roles, skills and gaps to set training, staffing and org priorities

steps.stem: Shop managers report that their baristas fear the new cloud tools, and no one has planned training or decided which roles will change. Which AWS CAF perspective should lead this work?

options.why: Business ties IT spending to business results and builds the business case, not staff training plans.
Governance aligns IT with business strategy and measures cloud investments, not how staff take the change.
People owns change management across the organization and reviews roles, skills and gaps to set training.
Platform designs the target architecture for workloads, and it does not plan staff training or role changes.

steps.takeaway: Moving a MySQL database onto Aurora for a gain, with no new code, is replatform, also called lift, tinker and shift.

read.text: A few cloud optimizations for a tangible gain, without new code or architecture changes

steps.stem: The cafe's loyalty database runs on MySQL on its own server. The database team wants to move it onto Amazon Aurora for better performance, without writing new code or changing the app's design. Which strategy is this?

options.why: Rehost moves the database exactly as it is, while switching to Aurora is a cloud optimization.
Refactor writes new code with cloud-built features, which this team is avoiding.
Relocate shifts existing VMs or containers to a cloud host, with no move onto a managed database.
Replatform makes a few cloud optimizations for a real gain, such as MySQL onto Aurora, with no new code.

steps.takeaway: Repurchase swaps licensed software for SaaS, often from a new vendor, and the new package can be slow to adopt and cost more upfront.

read.text: A database license dropped for cloud databases, or a CRM replaced by new sales force software; the new package can be slow to adopt and cost more upfront

steps.stem: The cafe will drop the licensed staff rota software it hosts itself and sign up for a SaaS rota tool from a new vendor. What should the owner expect from this choice?

options.text: It may have the team rewrite the rota code for cloud-built features
options.why: Rewriting code for cloud features is refactor, and a bought SaaS tool asks no code from the cafe.

options.text: It may keep paying for the old license and server for now
options.why: Keeping the old software and its license in place is retain, but this cafe is dropping that license.

options.text: It may take staff a while to adopt and cost more at the start
options.why: A new SaaS package from a new vendor can take staff a while to adopt and can cost more upfront.

options.text: It may carry the old software and its license over to AWS unchanged
options.why: Moving the same software over unchanged is rehost, while this cafe swaps it for a different product.

steps.takeaway: An app months from being shut down stays where it is under retain and is retired in place later.

read.text: Business-critical apps stay in the source environment for now: those needing major refactoring, work that can wait, or apps months from deprecation

steps.stem: The cafe's payroll app is still used every week, but it will be shut down a few months from now when its replacement arrives. The team sees no business sense in moving it first. Which strategy fits the app for now?

options.why: Retire switches off apps no longer needed, but payroll still runs every week until its replacement arrives.
Retain keeps an app in place for now, which suits one that is months from being shut down.
Rehost moves the app to AWS unchanged, effort the team sees no business sense in spending here.
Relocate moves existing VMs or containers to a cloud host, but the team does not want to move this app.
